title: Rooms Owner Anchor — payload
description: TODO: what the request payload of rooms/owner/anchor carries. The outer document members (id, type, issuer, recipient, issuedAt, expiresAt, proof) are owned by the framework — SPEC §6.3.

roomId.description: The room to anchor. The recipient MUST hold its group state and MUST be able to update its DID.

host.description:
The host to read the room's head from, as a DID.

The owner holds **one** of the three values it is about to publish. `rooms/epoch/mint`'s response is `{roomId, epoch}` — no watermark, and no reason there should be one: minting acts on the epoch, while the watermark and the commitment are facts about the room's *records*, which live at the host. So an anchor is assembled from a read, and this names where.

signingKeyId.description: The room's signing key, named rather than looked up: nothing maps a DID to its key, and a wrong key fails to verify against the room's own document at first use.

anchored.description: What was written — returned so an owner can see it without resolving their own room, and so an operator can compare it with what a member later reads.

versionId.description: The `did:webvh` log entry the anchor rode. This is what makes the anchor *witnessed*: naming the entry lets anyone fetch it and check the witnesses' signature over it.

reconciled.description:
Whether the host's own listing reconciled with the `recordCount` it committed to, at the moment this was read.

`false` is a host contradicting itself, and the anchor was still written — deliberately. An owner that refused to anchor a suspect room would leave it with no witnessed statement at all, which is the position the host benefits from. What is published is *what the host claimed*, and this member records that the owner had already caught it claiming something inconsistent.
